matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compare the left‑hand side with the right‑hand side to see how far the equality is off. This gives a target numeric difference that any stick move must resolve.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the puzzle, before trying any stick moves, to know the required numeric relationship.
matchstick.example: XVII = X - VII gives 17 on the left and 3 on the right, discrepancy = 14.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each numeral present, respecting stick orientation. This yields the possible value changes for each character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the set of possible value changes for each character.
matchstick.example: I → II (+1) by adding a vertical; X → V (−5) by removing a diagonal.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick, ensure the character you take it from remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and the character you add it to also becomes a valid one.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X leaves V, which is valid; adding that diagonal to V makes X, also valid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick can be moved from a V to make an X (value +5) or removed from an X to make a V (value −5). The rest of the symbol stays valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 5 and a V or X appears in the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing V to X raises the value by 5.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical from II yields I (value −1). Both source and result are valid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is 1 or when an I appears that could become II.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus, and adding a vertical to a minus creates a plus. This changes the arithmetic operation without altering other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by the value of the second operand and a plus or minus sign is present.
matchstick.example: Changing X – VII to X + VII adds the second operand, turning 3 into 17.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal stick, and vice versa. This prevents creating impossible symbols.
matchstick.example: A diagonal from X cannot be placed to form an I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify that it now holds. This catches moves that look plausible visually but do not balance the numbers.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each proposed transformation, before committing to an answer.
matchstick.example: After turning ‘-’ into ‘+’, recompute X + VII = 17.

matchstick.title: Swap horizontal sticks between operators
matchstick.principle: A horizontal stick can be moved from one operator to another (e.g., from ‘=’ to ‘-’), turning the source operator into a valid new operator (e.g., ‘=’ → ‘-’) and the destination into another valid operator (e.g., ‘-’ → ‘=’), while preserving a single equality sign somewhere in the final equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy cannot be fixed by numeral changes alone, consider moving a horizontal stick between the equality sign and another operator.
matchstick.example: Moving one bar from ‘=’ to ‘-’ changes ‘XVII = X - VII’ into ‘XVII - X = VII’, which balances the equation.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model confuses the visual shape of a slanted line with a vertical line, ignoring orientation constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce that stick orientation must be preserved; only vertical sticks can form I.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on achieving the target change and forgets to check that the source symbol remains a recognized numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the source character remains valid after a stick is taken away.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Operators are treated as immutable symbols, so the model does not consider adding or removing the vertical stick that changes ‘-’ to ‘+’ or vice versa.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include operator conversion in the enumeration of possible one‑stick moves.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes that fixing the visual layout automatically solves the puzzle, neglecting the need to recompute numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate transformation, recalculate the left‑hand and right‑hand values and check for equality.

matchstick.description: Assuming the equality sign cannot be altered
matchstick.why_it_happens: The rule “Never alter the equality sign” is over‑generalized, leading the model to discard valid moves that keep a proper ‘=’ sign elsewhere.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Allow moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ only if the final equation still contains a valid equality sign; treat ‘=’ as a mutable operator subject to the same source‑destination validation as other symbols.
